Welcome to Rokesly Juniors
Vision
As a whole school, we aim to provide an environment that is purposeful, creative, and dynamic – a place where children develop critical thinking, a lifelong thirst for learning, and reach their full potential through an academically ambitious curriculum.
We want pupils to grow into resourceful, independent learners, equipped with the knowledge and skills to succeed in the modern world. We see the acquisition of technological skills as a fundamental part of this.
We are committed to helping our pupils become confident and resilient individuals, both physically and emotionally, empowering them to make healthy, happy, and active life choices.
We strive for all of our pupils to make a positive contribution to the school and wider community. This will lay the foundations for them to become responsible global citizens of the future.
We aim for our school to be a place where individual strengths are nurtured, so that children can continue to achieve at an outstanding level to further strengthen our vision of excellence for all.​

The Rokesly Highlights
Thank you to all of the parents who came to the Art Exhibition yesterday evening. The children at Rokesly created a stunning collection of artwork, exploring the meaning of belonging, community and connection. The exhibition celebrated the idea that every child matters, every voice is valued and together we create…
Last half term, we were delighted to be selected to take part in the National Portrait Gallery’s Faces and Places programme. The project brought portraiture into our school and encouraged pupils to explore identity, place and community through art, discussion and creative activities. Every class in the juniors participated in a series…
A fantastic afternoon celebrating our School Travel Champions, inspiring active travel, healthy choices, and pupil leadership
Last Friday morning, Year 6 deepened their understanding of what life was like as an evacuee from London during World War Two. This learning linked closely to their history topic on World War Two and their English historical fiction text - Letters from the Lighthouse. The children also explored the experiences…
Year 4 children have completed their Bikeabilly course, marking a significant achievement in their journey towards becoming proficient cyclists. Safety, fun, and eco-friendly vibes all the way!
Our Year 5 children had a fantastic school trip to France. From exploring the French Christmas market to spending the day at a French school, it was a truly enriching experience. A heartfelt thank you to Career Legal for their generous donation.
Photos
You will notice that on our website we do not use full photographs of pupils. This is part of our commitment to safeguarding and protecting children’s privacy, helping us to maintain a safe and secure online environment for all members of our school community.
Please note that our instagram page is private and will require you to request access before being able to view our pages.

Headteacher’s Welcome
I am delighted to welcome you to our dynamic, vibrant and friendly school. We specialise in teaching children from ages 7-11 and offer an exceptional and immersive learning experience. Our children are inspired by a rich, broad and diverse curriculum that is complemented by an array of enrichment experiences, within and beyond the classroom.
We have high expectations and academic aspirations for our pupils and this is reflected in our school motto ‘working hard, aiming high and learning together’. We have excellent partnerships with our parents as we work together to develop our young people’s social skills, resilience and emotional literacy that will see them flourish throughout their lifetime as lifelong learners.
Our dedicated team of teaching and support staff work ambitiously to deliver a tailored curriculum, ensuring that the individual talents and interests of all our pupils are discovered and nurtured. The opportunities are endless, from learning to play a musical instrument such as guitar, trumpet, clarinet or violin to learning French.
The physical and mental wellbeing of our pupils are paramount: we are a healthy school and offer a wide range of extra-curricular clubs and sporting activities including dance mindfulness, tag rugby, dodge ball and multi sports.
Our pupils also benefit from educational trips and visits and take part in adventurous outdoor activities.
Our involvement in cutting edge projects and initiatives allows us to provide aspirational experiences for our pupils to develop their life skills: confidence, self-belief, independence and resourcefulness. We are actively involved in community, cultural outreach and national projects and we regularly host visitors from the arts and creative world including poets, artists, actors, illustrators, chefs and even the former Children’s Laureate.
Our pupils have shared their ideas with the Mayor of Haringey, been pioneers as part of a nationwide architectural learning programme with the Royal Institute of British Architects and won national and local competitions.
Our strong transition and induction programme supports our pupils as they move seamlessly from the successful and popular Rokesly Infants, located in the same spacious grounds, and then on to high quality local secondary schools equipped with the skills, knowledge and experiences for future success.
We have been established for almost 70 years and are a happy, high achieving school where our pupils thrive and are excited to learn and grow; we know that their thirst for learning stays with them throughout their lives.
Please follow us on Instagram to get a snapshot into life at our school @RokeslyJunior.
If you want to find out more and want to meet our wonderful children and staff, you’re warmly invited to book an appointment – we can’t wait to show you round.
Bola Soneye-ThomasHeadteacher

French
Our intention is that pupils will make substantial progress in a language which will lay the foundations for further study in Key stage 3 and beyond. The curriculum balances spoken and written language appropriately with the focus on practical communication. Pupils listen attentively and are able to show their understanding by joining in and responding. The curriculum allows pupils to present their ideas orally to an audience and show their understanding of words and phrases when reading.
In line with our school vision we want all our children to know about the wider world and how we are all connected. As part of our International School status, we have a long-term partnership with a school in rural France. This allows all children at Rokesly to develop their French language skills and to learn more about another culture. Also allowing for children at Rokesly the opportunity to share their experiences of school life in London. The children meet on-line and via regular letters to their pen pals. French Curriculum Map
Year 5 Trip to France!
Last week, Year 5 embarked on an unforgettable adventure to Lille, France, and what an incredible experience it was! From visiting a local school and making new friends to exploring the magical Christmas market filled with festive delights, the trip was packed with excitement and learning. 🎄🎁 The journey itself was a highlight as they travelled through the iconic Euro Tunnel, an amazing experience in itself! 🚄🌍 The day was filled with laughter, discovery, and memories that will last a lifetime. A huge well done to Year 5 for embracing this cultural experience with so much enthusiasm!

Wraparound Care
Wraparound care- JFC
Children are looked after by our experienced school staff, meaning they are always supported by familiar, trusted adults in a safe and nurturing environment. Importantly, our wraparound provision is able to accommodate all children who need a place, ensuring families can rely on consistent, dependable care without having to worry about waiting lists.
At Breakfast Club, children enjoy a healthy, nutritious breakfast and gentle, calming activities to help them feel relaxed and ready to learn. After school, they can refuel with a snack, take part in fun indoor and outdoor play, or enjoy some quiet reading time to read or relax.
With a welcoming atmosphere, enriching activities, and competitive pricing, our wraparound care offers families flexible, high-quality support they can rely on.
Induction and Settling In
We understand that starting a new club can feel like a big step for children and parents.
All children joining Rokesly Wraparound Care will be supported through a gentle induction process helping them to become familiar with:
Staff will take time to support children individually, ensuring they feel comfortable, confident and happy in the setting from the very start.

Bookings are made online, and places can be booked up to 2.30 pm on the same day via SCOPAY. A unique link for parents to register for this platform is available from the school offices. Book Now
Cancellations and Late Bookings
Emergencies happen and the school is flexible, however after the third late pick-up the booking system will restrict further bookings.

PE and Sport Premium for Primary Schools
In April 2013, the Government announced new funding of £150 million for physical education (PE) and sport, to be used to improve the quality and breadth of PE and sport provision. Funding has been allocated yearly to all maintained and state-funded schools with primary phase pupils from 1 September 2013.
Schools are free to determine how best to use this funding to improve the quality and breadth of PE and sport provision, including increasing participation in PE and sport so that all pupils develop healthy lifestyles and reach the performance levels they are capable of.

It provides children with the opportunities to develop in a range of ways in which they can share and express their individual creativity, whilst learning about and making links with a wide spectrum of different types of art in our society. The teaching of art enables pupils to develop a natural sense of wonder and curiosity about the world around them.

Computing
At Rokesly, we know that knowledge and understanding of technology is of increasing importance for children’s future both at home and for employment. Therefore, we aim to prepare our learners for their future by providing them with a modern, ambitious and relevant education in computing. We want to equip pupils to use computational thinking and creativity that will enable them to become active participants in the digital world. It is important that children have opportunities to gain knowledge and develop skills they need to use technology safely and creatively in an ever changing and developing digital world.
Our curriculum meets the interests of all learners, sequenced with a range of creative learning experiences and challenges based on the essential requirements of the computing programme of study. We ensure learning is embedded and children can build on their understanding, as each new concept and skill is taught with opportunities for children to revisit skills and knowledge as they progress through the school.

We teach the National Curriculum, supported by a clear skills and knowledge progression. This ensures that skills and knowledge are built on year by year and sequenced appropriately to maximise learning for all children.

English
Reading plays an important part in this as it not only enables pupils to acquire and build on knowledge and intellect, but also through well-chosen texts expands vocabulary and horizons and inspires pupils to develop culturally, emotionally, socially and spiritually. We have developed a curriculum that introduces a rich and varied range of texts that reference our great literacy heritage but also draws on modern and global authors to enable us to represent the multi-cultural society we live in and provide opportunities to discuss important issues and moral dilemmas, challenging stereotypes and discrimination.
We believe that children should be confident and fluent in writing for a variety of purposes and aim to provide ‘real life’ opportunities for them to experience the power of written communication. We nurture a culture where children take pride in their writing, adapting their language and style for a range of contexts and understanding that writing can often be a long and complex process where stamina and self-reflection are needed.
We place a great deal of emphasis on speaking and listening and our aim is for all children to be confident in presenting, discussion, debating, asking and answering questions. Listening and responding to the opinions of others is regarded as important as speaking.

Geography
Through the teaching of Geography at Rokesly Junior School we aim for all pupils to be inspired to be both curious and fascinated by the world around them and the people within it. We aim for all children to leave our school with the foundations to be independent, resourceful learners who are equipped with the knowledge of the diverse spaces, people, resources and physical and human process. Through the teaching of a purposeful, dynamic geography curriculum in line with the National Curriculum, children will have a growing knowledge of the Earth’s physical and human processes and how they are interconnected. The children will develop the knowledge of the location of globally significant places and understand the process that give rise to the human physical features of the world. They will learn and use a range of geographical skills that will in turn will deepen their understanding of geographical processes. Throughout the curriculum children have the opportunity to take their knowledge out into the field to develop their geographical thinking and skills. The children will leave with a deep understanding of changes over time and how people have influenced the physical world and how everyone can make changes to the future of it, resulting in the children of Rokesly Junior school becoming responsible global citizens.

History
At Rokesly Junior School we want all children to have a thirst for learning and to develop their understanding of the world and their place within it. Through our dynamic and creative sequential history curriculum, in line with the National Curriculum, children will learn the foundations of how the past informs the present and how it can influence the future. The children will develop the understanding of the fascinating complexity of people’s lives throughout history from the earliest of times right through to the present day, enabling them to ask perceptive questions, think critically, weigh evidence, sift arguments and develop perspective and judgement.
Through the acquisition of the knowledge and skills, children will be able to understand significant aspects of the history of the United Kingdom and the wider world. Throughout curriculum, the children will ask challenging historical questions about periods of time and link their knowledge through both overview and depth studies of periods in history. Ultimately, leaving our school with the foundations to continue to be independent, resourceful learners.
